beats: Hook: DeepSeek-V3 trained on 2,048 GPUs with no tensor parallelism at all; why skip the most famous trick? (line_dials_engineer turning one knob of four all the way down, the cover).
The four dials (slide 29): DP and CP cut the inputs, TP and PP cut the model; each run is one setting of four knobs (line_dials_four_knob_desk, pointers drawn by pen; reuse line_knob_board).

The rule (slide 30), ranked by how much each one talks: TP chats all the time, so it stays inside one node (line_dials_chatty_desk); PP hands work across nodes (line_dials_window_handoff); CP for long sequences; DP talks once per step and scales the rest (line_dials_daily_letter).
Nemotron-4 340B on 6,144 H100s (slide 31): TP 8, PP 12 interleaved, DP 16-64 with ZeRO-1, 4k sequences (the knob desk; reuse line_d_servers).

DeepSeek-V3 on 2,048 GPUs (slide 32): PP 16 (DualPipe), EP 64, DP 2, no TP; careful memory savings make TP unnecessary and leave the links free for the experts' all-to-all traffic (line_dials_narrow_bridge; reuse line_d_chefs for the experts); its sequence length grows in stages, 4K to 32K to 128K. Keep it technical and neutral: check the reason against the report, no talk of where chips may be sold.

Llama 3 405B on 16,384 H100s (slide 33): pipeline-data co-design, and context parallelism switched on only for the long-context stage (line_dials_long_scroll_knob: the engineer turns the CP knob up as the scroll gets long).

MegaScale 175B on 12,288 GPUs at 55.2% MFU (slides 34-36): talk while you work, fused AllGather+GEMM and decoupled send/receive (line_dials_cook_while_talking); at that scale machines fail, so cluster management matters (slide 37; line_dials_swap_broken_server).

Coda (slides 38-42, self study): packing documents of different lengths makes the 4D work uneven again (WLB-LLM, OSDI 2025) (line_dials_packing_bins; line_ring_lopsided_work from L07-02 if it is in the library).
Takeaway: the same four dials, set by how much each one talks; closes the training season.

drawings.name: line_dials_four_knob_desk
drawings.prompt: A wide vintage mixing desk seen straight from the front and slightly from above: a sturdy console with wooden sides and exactly four very large chunky round knobs in one evenly spaced row, each knob on its own round plate with a ring of short tick marks around its lower three quarters, and a blank rectangular label plate under each knob. The knob tops are plain circles with NO pointer line and NO notch (pointers are added later). A few small plain toggle switches along the bottom edge. Landscape image 1536x1024; the desk fills about 92% of the width and about 55% of the height, centred. No text, no letters, no numbers on the labels or anywhere.

drawings.name: line_dials_engineer
drawings.prompt: An invented sound engineer (simple round face, dot eyes, a short bob haircut, big headphones around the neck, a plain t-shirt with rolled sleeves) leans over a vintage mixing desk with exactly four big round knobs, seen from the front and slightly above; one hand turns the leftmost knob all the way down, the other hand rests on the desk; a thoughtful, determined look; a mug at the edge of the desk. Portrait image 1024x1536; the engineer and the desk fill about 85% of the width and about 80% of the height, the four knobs large and clearly visible. No text, no letters, no numbers.

drawings.name: line_dials_chatty_desk
drawings.prompt: Two invented coworkers (simple round faces, dot eyes; one with short messy hair and round glasses, one with a high ponytail) sit very close together at one small shared desk, seen from the front, both talking at once and passing papers back and forth, with many small blank speech bubbles popping up above them. Square image 1024x1024; the pair and the desk fill about 85% of the width and about 80% of the height. The speech bubbles and papers are blank: no text, no letters, no numbers.

drawings.name: line_dials_window_handoff
drawings.prompt: Two neighbouring buildings side by side with a narrow gap between them, seen from the front. In two facing windows at the same height, an invented worker in the left window (simple round face, dot eyes, a cap worn backwards, a hoodie) hands a closed cardboard box across the gap to an invented worker in the right window (simple round face, dot eyes, short curly hair, a cardigan) who reaches out to take it; behind each of them, inside, a workbench. Landscape image 1536x1024; the two buildings fill about 85% of the width and about 85% of the height. No signs, no text, no letters, no numbers.

Portrait image 1024x1536; the worker and the post box fill about 75% of the width and about 80% of the height. The envelope is blank, the post box has no emblem and no symbols. drawings.name: line_dials_long_scroll_knob
drawings.prompt: An invented sound engineer (simple round face, dot eyes, a short bob haircut, big headphones around the neck, a plain t-shirt with rolled sleeves) stands at a vintage mixing desk with exactly four big round knobs in one row, seen from the front and slightly above. A very long blank paper scroll comes in over the top of the desk from the left, unrolling across it in loose loops and spilling down to the floor; the engineer glances at the growing scroll and, with one hand, turns the rightmost knob firmly up, a pleased, decisive look.
